1. Purpose
This document defines the methodology for classifying demand trends for chemical commodities.

2. Data Source

4. Thresholds for Trend Classification
The trend is determined by the average period-over-period change (in tons) over the 8-month period.
- strong_growth: Average change > +50 tons
- mild_growth: Average change > 0 and <= +50 tons
- flat: Average change between -20 and +20 tons (inclusive)
- mild_decline: Average change >= -50 and < -20 tons
- strong_decline: Average change < -50 tons

We are confident that the LCAS risk profile has been mitigated to an acceptable level, aligning with our strategic goal of zero-breach operations.    * Risk Title: Unauthorized Access to Claimant PII via Legacy Session Tokens
   * Inherent Likelihood (1-5 Scale): The assessment notes that '5 represents the highest probability of occurrence.' Management has recorded the Inherent Likelihood as 5, citing the high volume of daily logins.
   * Inherent Impact (1-5 Scale): The assessment notes that '5 represents the most severe financial and reputational damage.' Management has recorded the Inherent Impact as 5, citing the potential for class-action litigation.
   * Inherent Risk Score: 5 x 5 = 25.

3. Control Environment
   * Control ID: CT-091: Mandatory Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for all external interfaces.

Impact level = the highest level reached across all dimensions.

--- EVENT SUMMARY ---

Audit identified a systematic underpricing error in the commercial property book for the Queensland market. The pricing algorithm used an incorrect flood-risk load factor of 0.3% instead of the correct 1.2% for Category C flood zones, applied to all new and renewal policies issued between 1 July 2023 and 31 January 2025 (19 months).

Scope of affected policies: 6,847 commercial property policies in Queensland, all in Category C flood zones. Affected policyholders were under-charged by an average of AUD 1,840 per policy per year.

Financial impact:
  • Cumulative premium under-collection: AUD 12,598,480
  • Reinsurance recovery (per treaty): The underpriced premiums fall below the treaty attachment point, so no reinsurance recovery applies.
  • Claims exposure: The audit notes that 6 flood claims have been filed in the affected period, totalling AUD 4,200,000 in paid claims. Had premiums been correctly priced, the loss ratio would have been within normal range; the underpricing itself does not increase claim frequency or severity but reduces the premium base against which claims are measured.
  • Total financial impact = premium under-collection (no recovery) = AUD 12,598,480.

Exchange rate (RBA reference, 2025-02-10): 1 AUD = 0.65 USD.
  USD equivalent of AUD 12,598,480 = $8,189,012.

Additional financial item: The audit also identified a separate currency-trading loss on the Queensland book's hedging position of CAD 85,000 incurred when the AUD/CAD hedge was unwound. Exchange rate: 1 CAD = 0.74 USD. USD equivalent = $62,900. This is included in the total financial impact.

Revised total financial impact: $8,189,012 + $62,900 = $8,251,912.

Regulatory: The underpricing error constitutes a breach of prudential standard CPS 220 (Risk Management). APRA (Australian Prudential Regulation Authority) has been notified and has opened a formal investigation. The insurer's chief actuary has been asked to provide a remediation plan within 30 days. APRA has indicated potential enforcement action including the possibility of a licence condition imposition, though no formal licence suspension has been issued. The potential loss of licence to underwrite new business in Queensland has been flagged by APRA as a possible outcome pending investigation findings.

Customer impact: 6,847 policyholders are affected. Affected policyholders will receive communications about premium adjustments at renewal. No policyholder claims have been denied; coverage remains in force. No policyholders have lodged complaints to date.

Reputational: The story has been covered in the Australian Financial Review (national financial newspaper) and was picked up by Bloomberg, resulting in international wire distribution. S&P Global Ratings placed the insurer's AA- rating on CreditWatch Negative. Moody's issued a similar watch notice. Two senior underwriting executives (Queensland State Manager and Head of Commercial Property) have resigned.

Remediation costs: AUD 180,000 for system fix, policyholder communications, and actuarial review. USD equivalent: $117,000. This is additional to the financial impact above.

Grand total financial impact including remediation: $8,251,912 + $117,000 = $8,368,912.

Insurance: The company holds a professional indemnity policy with a $2,000,000 deductible. No PI claim has been filed yet; the audit assesses that filing a PI claim for pricing errors is unlikely to succeed as the error is operational and not a professional service failure covered by the PI policy. No insurance recovery expected.
